key.name: saved-originals
key.summary: Saved originals of GNOME settings Guava changed (internal)
key.description: JSON written by core/originals.js: the user's own value of every GNOME setting Guava currently owns (for example the window button-layout), so it can be put back after a crash. Do not edit.

key.name: saved-originals-backup
key.description: Internal. The text of saved-originals when it could not be parsed, kept so a damaged store is never silently lost. Do not edit.

key.name: onboarding
key.description: Internal. "new": the Setup Assistant was never offered; Guava opens it once, after the session has started. "requested": Guava opened the preferences for it. "shown": it is up. "done": finished or skipped. Run it again from Guava Settings > About.

key.name: menubar-show-activities
key.description: Show GNOME's Activities button (the workspace pill) at the left of the menu bar. Off, as on macOS: the menu bar starts with the logo menu.

key.name: menubar-logo
key.description: The logo at the left end of the menu bar, which opens the logo menu (About This PC, System Settings, Force Quit, Sleep, Restart, Shut Down, Lock Screen, Log Out). "fedora" shows the system's logo, "guava" Guava's, "none" removes the logo menu.

key.name: menubar-app-menu
key.description: Show the focused app's name in bold and its menus (App, File, Edit, View, Window, Help) after the logo, as on macOS.

key.name: menubar-native-menus
key.description: Show the menus an app exports in place of the generic File, Edit and View: GTK menu bars (org.gtk.Menus) and DBusMenu menu bars from Qt, Electron, LibreOffice and other X11 apps. While on, Guava runs the com.canonical.AppMenu.Registrar service unless another program already does.

key.name: menubar-atspi-menus
key.description: For apps with no exported menus, read the menu bar in the focused window from the accessibility tree (AT-SPI) and invoke its items from there.

key.name: menubar-atspi-popovers
key.summary: Read primary menus of apps without a menu bar (experimental)
key.description: With accessibility menus on, open the primary menu (the ☰ button) of apps without a menu bar out of sight, read its items into the app menu, and remember them per app. The app sees its menu open and close. Needs the accessibility bus, which GNOME starts on demand; Guava never changes the toolkit-accessibility setting.

key.name: menubar-transparent
key.description: The menu bar is transparent over the wallpaper, and its text turns dark or light by the wallpaper's brightness under it. Off shows the menu bar background all the time.

key.name: menubar-solid-on-window
key.summary: Solid menu bar when a window touches it
key.description: Off (the default, as on macOS): the transparent menu bar stays transparent over maximized windows. On: it turns solid while a window touches it or is maximized.

key.name: menubar-fullscreen-visible
key.summary: Always show the menu bar in full screen
key.description: Off, as on macOS: the menu bar hides over full-screen windows and slides in when the pointer touches the top edge. On keeps it shown.

key.name: menubar-privacy-dots
key.description: Show an orange dot while an app uses the microphone, a green one for the camera and a purple one while the screen is shared or recorded, in place of GNOME's privacy icons. Click a dot to see which app.

key.name: menubar-command-glyphs
key.description: Write shortcuts in menus with macOS symbols (⌘ for Super, ⌃ Control, ⌥ Alt, ⇧ Shift). Off writes them in words (Super+H).

key.name: menubar-clock-option-dnd
key.summary: Alt-click the clock for Do Not Disturb
key.description: Alt-clicking the clock turns Do Not Disturb on or off, like Option-click on macOS.

key.name: menubar-focus-shortcut
key.description: Opens the app menu so the menus can be used with the keyboard (Left and Right move between menus), like Ctrl+F2 on macOS. F10 is the other common choice, but it takes F10 from apps. Empty means no shortcut.

key.name: menubar-force-quit-shortcut
key.description: Opens the Force Quit Applications window. Empty means no shortcut.

key.name: move-calendar-right
key.description: Move the calendar to the right side of the top panel and hide the notifications panel.

key.name: keep-notification-panel
key.description: When Move Calendar to Right is enabled, keep the native notification/calendar combined layout (only the panel position changes).

key.name: notification-indicator-style
key.description: Color style of the top-panel notification indicator dot: default (red), accent (follows accent color), or symbolic (theme foreground).

key.name: custom-dnd-button
key.description: Replace the system Do Not Disturb quick settings button with Guava's custom implementation.

key.name: dock
key.description: Guava's own macOS-style dock: pinned apps (GNOME favourites), running and recent apps, a Downloads stack and the Trash. Dash to Dock is turned off while it runs and turned back on after.

key.name: dock-position
key.description: The screen edge the dock sits on: bottom, left or right.

key.name: dock-icon-size
key.description: Size of the dock's icons in pixels.

key.name: dock-autohide
key.summary: Automatically hide and show the Dock
key.description: Hide the dock until the pointer rests on, or pushes against, its screen edge. Windows may then use the whole screen.

key.name: dock-autohide-delay
key.description: Milliseconds the pointer rests on the edge before the hidden dock shows. Pushing against the edge shows it at once.

key.name: dock-show-recents
key.summary: Show suggested and recent apps in Dock
key.description: Keep up to three recently used apps that are not pinned in their own section after the pinned apps.

key.name: dock-recent-apps
key.description: Internal. The recently used unpinned apps the dock shows, newest first. Written by the dock.

key.name: dock-running-dots
key.description: A small dot under the icon of every running app.

key.name: dock-minimize-to-app
key.description: Minimized windows go into their app's icon. Off: each minimized window gets its own tile next to the Downloads stack.

key.name: dock-minimize-effect
key.description: The effect that takes a window into the Dock and back: genie (the magic lamp, the macOS default), scale (a plain shrink) or gnome (GNOME's own). Reduced motion turns both into a fade.

key.name: dock-magnification
key.description: Icons under the pointer grow, with a smooth falloff to their neighbours (off by default, as on macOS).

key.name: dock-magnification-size
key.description: Size in pixels of the icon right under the pointer while magnification is on (never smaller than the Dock's icons).

key.name: dock-launch-animation
key.description: An app's icon bounces while the app starts.

key.name: dock-attention-bounce
key.description: An app's icon bounces when one of its windows asks for attention or the app marks itself urgent.

key.name: dock-badges
key.summary: Show badges and progress on Dock icons
key.description: Red counts and progress bars that apps publish through the LauncherEntry D-Bus API (com.canonical.Unity.LauncherEntry).

key.name: dock-background-apps
key.summary: Show apps running in the background
key.description: Apps with no window that run in the background (the Background portal list GNOME's Quick Settings show) appear in the Dock with a grey dot.

key.name: dock-folders
key.description: Folders kept in the Dock as stacks, beside the Downloads stack (absolute paths). Drag a folder to the right side of the Dock to add one.

key.name: dock-downloads
key.description: Show the Downloads folder before the Trash; click it to see the newest files.

key.name: dock-downloads-view
key.description: How the Downloads stack opens: automatic (a fan for a few files from a bottom dock, else a grid), fan, grid or list.

key.name: dock-mission-control
key.description: Shows a Mission Control item in the dock, next to the apps. Off by default, as on macOS.

key.name: button-size
key.description: Size of the macOS traffic lights in app titlebars (small: 14px, normal: 16px).

key.name: window-controls-side
key.description: Which side of the apps' own titlebars holds the close, minimize and maximize buttons (the GNOME window button-layout, which Guava sets and restores). 'right' (default) is the GNOME side: minimize, maximize, close. 'left' is the macOS side: close, minimize, maximize. Window buttons always stay on the app's titlebar; Guava draws none in the top bar.

key.name: app-buttons-style
key.description: 'gnome' leaves the apps' buttons in the stock libadwaita/GTK look, 'macos' applies Guava's traffic-light GTK CSS (see button-size). Open apps pick up a change when restarted.

key.name: app-buttons-set
key.description: Which buttons the apps show in their own titlebar, on the side window-controls-side names: 'all' (close, minimize and maximize) or 'close' only (the stock Fedora layout).

key.name: move-window-to-new-workspace
key.description: Enable or disable moving windows to new workspaces.

key.name: rounded-corners
key.description: Round the corners of normal and dialog windows (see rounded-corners-which). Maximized, tiled and fullscreen windows keep square corners.

key.name: rounded-corners-which
key.description: 'top' rounds the top-left and top-right corners and keeps the bottom ones square; 'all' rounds all four.

key.name: rounded-corners-radius
key.description: Radius of the rounded window corners, in logical pixels.

key.name: rounded-corners-blacklist
key.description: Windows whose WM_CLASS or app id (for example "org.gnome.Terminal" or "firefox") is listed keep square corners. Not case-sensitive.

key.name: windows-tiling
key.description: Guava tiles windows the way macOS 15 does: by dragging to the screen edges, corners, menu bar and the snap layouts at the top centre, and with keyboard shortcuts. While it runs, GNOME's own edge tiling (org.gnome.mutter edge-tiling) is off; the user's value is saved and restored.

key.name: windows-tile-drag-edges
key.summary: Drag windows to screen edges to tile
key.description: Drag a window to the left or right edge for a half, or to a corner for a quarter. A translucent outline shows the tile; releasing tiles the window.

key.name: windows-tile-drag-menubar
key.summary: Drag windows to menu bar to fill screen
key.description: Drag a window onto the top bar to fill the screen (without full screen).

key.name: windows-tile-drag-picker
key.summary: Snap layouts at the top centre while dragging
key.description: Dragging a window to the top edge at the centre of the screen slides a handle down under the top bar (Windows 11 Snap Layouts). Moving onto the handle expands it into a bar of layouts (halves, thirds, quarters); releasing over a zone tiles the window there, releasing elsewhere on the bar does nothing.

key.name: windows-tile-drag-modifier
key.summary: Hold Alt while dragging windows to tile
key.description: While Alt (the macOS Option key) is held during a drag, the half outlines show at once, without reaching the edge.

key.name: windows-tile-margins
key.description: Leave a small margin around and between tiled windows. Off by default, as on macOS.

key.name: windows-tile-left-shortcut
key.description: Move the focused window to the left half of the screen. A shortcut that GNOME or another active Guava shortcut already uses is left unbound.

key.name: windows-tile-right-shortcut
key.description: Move the focused window to the right half of the screen. A shortcut that GNOME or another active Guava shortcut already uses is left unbound.

key.name: windows-tile-top-shortcut
key.description: Move the focused window to the top half of the screen. A shortcut that GNOME or another active Guava shortcut already uses is left unbound.

key.name: windows-tile-bottom-shortcut
key.description: Move the focused window to the bottom half of the screen. Left unbound while Stage Manager uses the same shortcut. A shortcut that GNOME or another active Guava shortcut already uses is left unbound.

key.name: windows-fill-shortcut
key.description: Fill the screen with the focused window, without full screen. A shortcut that GNOME or another active Guava shortcut already uses is left unbound.

key.name: windows-center-shortcut
key.description: Centre the focused window on the screen. A shortcut that GNOME or another active Guava shortcut already uses is left unbound.

key.name: windows-restore-shortcut
key.description: Put the focused window back where it was before it was tiled. A shortcut that GNOME or another active Guava shortcut already uses is left unbound.

key.name: windows-arrange-left-right-shortcut
key.description: The focused window on the left half, the previous window on the right half. A shortcut that GNOME or another active Guava shortcut already uses is left unbound.

key.name: windows-arrange-right-left-shortcut
key.description: The focused window on the right half, the previous window on the left half. A shortcut that GNOME or another active Guava shortcut already uses is left unbound.

key.name: windows-arrange-top-bottom-shortcut
key.description: The focused window on the top half, the previous window on the bottom half. A shortcut that GNOME or another active Guava shortcut already uses is left unbound.

key.name: windows-arrange-bottom-top-shortcut
key.description: The focused window on the bottom half, the previous window on the top half. A shortcut that GNOME or another active Guava shortcut already uses is left unbound.

key.name: windows-arrange-left-quarters-shortcut
key.description: The focused window on the left half, the next two windows in the right quarters. A shortcut that GNOME or another active Guava shortcut already uses is left unbound.

key.name: windows-arrange-right-quarters-shortcut
key.description: The focused window on the right half, the next two windows in the left quarters. A shortcut that GNOME or another active Guava shortcut already uses is left unbound.

key.name: windows-arrange-top-quarters-shortcut
key.description: The focused window on the top half, the next two windows in the bottom quarters. A shortcut that GNOME or another active Guava shortcut already uses is left unbound.

key.name: windows-arrange-bottom-quarters-shortcut
key.description: The focused window on the bottom half, the next two windows in the top quarters. A shortcut that GNOME or another active Guava shortcut already uses is left unbound.

key.name: windows-app-hide
key.description: Hide an app (Super+H, or Hide in the app menu): its windows are minimized without the minimize effect and come back together when the app is activated again. Hide Others hides every other app.

key.name: windows-hide-shortcut
key.description: Hides the focused app. While it is GNOME's minimize shortcut (Super+H by default), Guava takes it from GNOME's minimize binding and gives it back on disable.

key.name: windows-hide-others-shortcut
key.description: Hides every app except the focused one.

key.name: overview-gestures-workspace-only
key.summary: Swipe up only to the workspace overview
key.description: The overview swipe (three fingers on the touchpad or the touchscreen) stops at the workspace overview and never goes on into the app grid. The app grid stays on the apps button, Super+A and the Launchpad.

key.name: disable-hot-corner
key.description: No hot corner opens the overview while Guava runs. The GNOME setting enable-hot-corners is left as it is and applies again when this is off.

key.name: liquid-glass
key.description: Faux Liquid Glass on every Guava surface: a translucent tint with a sheen, a rim and a soft shadow; no blur. Off keeps the theme's solid surfaces.

key.name: liquid-glass-surfaces
key.description: Which surfaces use glass: panel, menus, dock, overlays.

key.name: glass-tint
key.description: 0 is Clear, the macOS default: the most see-through glass that keeps text readable. 100 is Tinted: more opaque glass. Has no effect while Reduce Transparency or Increase Contrast is on.

key.name: glass-wallpaper-tint
key.description: Mix a little of the wallpaper's average colour into the glass, like macOS. The wallpaper is sampled once each time it changes.

key.name: glass-noise
key.description: Add a faint grain to the glass, so it reads as frosted. Replaces the top-to-bottom sheen (St draws one or the other).

key.name: glass-reduce-transparency
key.description: Make every Guava glass surface opaque, without the wallpaper tint. The rim stays.

key.name: glass-increase-contrast
key.description: Opaque, flat surfaces with strong borders. Implies Reduce Transparency. GNOME's High Contrast does the same.

key.name: glass-show-borders
key.description: Draw a clearly visible border around every Guava glass surface, so overlapping surfaces stay apart.

key.name: appearance-auto
key.description: Switch between Light by day and Dark by night (GNOME's color-scheme). Guava switches only while you are idle, and puts your own choice back when this is off. Choosing a style yourself turns Auto off.

key.name: appearance-auto-schedule
key.description: "sun": Dark from sunset to sunrise (from the location GNOME's Night Light last saw, else your time zone). "custom": the two times below.

key.name: appearance-auto-light-minute
key.description: Custom schedule: when Light begins, in minutes after midnight (420 = 07:00).

key.name: appearance-auto-dark-minute
key.description: Custom schedule: when Dark begins, in minutes after midnight (1140 = 19:00).

key.name: appearance-accent
key.description: "multicolor" (the macOS default) follows the GNOME accent colour and leaves it alone. Any other value sets GNOME's accent-color while Guava runs (graphite is GNOME's slate) and gives yours back when Guava stops.

key.name: appearance-highlight
key.description: The text selection colour in Guava's search fields (Spotlight, clipboard). "accent" follows the accent colour, the macOS default.

key.name: macos-text-rendering
key.description: Draw text unhinted with grayscale antialiasing, as macOS does. Sets GNOME's font-hinting and font-antialiasing while Guava runs and gives yours back when it stops. Choosing another rendering in GNOME Tweaks turns this off.

key.name: macos-font
key.description: Use SF Pro when installed, else Inter, as the interface and document font at your own size (and SF Mono as the monospace font when installed). Nothing changes while neither is installed. Your fonts come back when this goes off or Guava stops; choosing another font in GNOME Tweaks turns this off.

key.name: appearance-icon-style
key.description: The look of app icons Guava draws (dock, Spotlight, switcher, Launchpad), as in macOS Tahoe: Default, Dark (darker icons), Clear (decolourised, translucent) or Tinted (in the accent colour).

key.name: popup-menu-styling
key.description: Restyle shell popup menus with taller items and accent-colored hover, selected and checked entries, and apply the GTK 3 and GTK 4 app fixes (fixes3.css, fixes4.css).

key.name: input-indicator
key.description: Show a small badge at the text cursor when Caps Lock or the input source changes (macOS Sonoma). Near the pointer when the app does not report its cursor.

key.name: input-indicator-caps-lock
key.description: Show the Caps Lock badge at the text cursor when Caps Lock is turned on or off.

key.name: input-indicator-source
key.description: Show the new input source (for example EN or DE) at the text cursor when it changes.

key.name: emoji-picker
key.description: A searchable emoji popover at the text cursor that types the chosen emoji into the focused app (macOS Character Viewer).

key.name: emoji-shortcut
key.description: Opens the emoji popover (macOS: Control-Command-Space). Empty means no shortcut.

key.name: emoji-skin-tone
key.description: 0 is the default yellow; 1 to 5 are light to dark. Set from the popover.

key.name: emoji-recents
key.description: Written by the emoji popover, newest first. Kept only in your settings.

key.name: control-center
key.description: Re-lay out the Quick Settings menu like the macOS Control Center: blocks for connectivity, focus, display, sound and media, with Stage Manager and Liquid Glass tiles. GNOME keeps running every toggle. Off restores the stock menu.

key.name: control-center-user-row
key.description: Show your picture and name in the Control Center footer, with the battery time left. Replaces the old username label in the top bar (add-username-to-quick-menu, migrated).

key.name: battery-percentage-always
key.description: Show the battery charge in the top bar at any level, not only when it is low. Not shown while GNOME's own battery percentage is on.

key.name: control-center-layout
key.description: The controls of the Control Center in order, each "id:size" (small, medium or large), as arranged with Edit Controls. Empty means Guava's default arrangement. Controls left out are hidden; other extensions' items are always kept.

key.name: low-power-battery
key.description: Hold the power-saver profile of power-profiles-daemon while the computer runs on battery. The hold is released on power or when Guava stops, so GNOME's own choice comes back.

key.name: low-power-adapter
key.summary: Low Power Mode on power adapter
key.description: Hold the power-saver profile while the computer is plugged in (or has no battery).

key.name: menubar-status-items
key.description: Show apps' status icons (StatusNotifierItem tray icons: Discord, Steam, Nextcloud...) in the menu bar with their menus. When the AppIndicator extension is enabled, it draws them and Guava only hides and orders them.

key.name: menubar-pinned
key.description: Control Center controls shown in the menu bar, each "id=always" or "id=active" (only while active). Ids: wifi, bluetooth, sound, battery, focus, now-playing, keyboard-brightness, screen-recording.

key.name: menubar-battery-percentage
key.summary: Battery percentage in the menu bar
key.description: Show the charge next to the pinned Battery item (macOS shows no percentage by default).

key.name: menubar-item-order
key.description: The order of the managed menu bar items, left to right (pin:wifi, sni:discord, stock:keyboard...). New items go first.

key.name: menubar-item-hidden
key.description: Managed menu bar items the user hid.

key.name: menubar-item-registry
key.description: Written by Guava: the items it has seen ("id title"), so the preferences can list them.

key.name: menubar-overflow
key.description: When the menu bar is crowded, put the items that do not fit behind a chevron.

key.name: stage-manager
key.description: Show the other apps as live, stacked thumbnails in a strip at the screen edge. Click one to switch to it. While Stage Manager is on, Minimize to Dock, window tiling by drag and Move Fullscreen Window are paused (their settings are kept).

key.name: stage-manager-side
key.description: Which screen edge holds the strip: "left" or "right". With the dock on the left or right edge, the strip always takes the other side.

key.name: stage-manager-autohide
key.description: Hide the strip while a window on the stage overlaps it, and show it again when the pointer pushes against the screen edge.

key.name: stage-manager-group-by-app
key.summary: Show an app's windows all at once
key.description: On ("All at Once", macOS default): an app's windows come onto the stage together and share one strip entry; a new window joins its app on the stage. Off ("One at a Time"): each window is its own entry, and a new window gets its own stage.

key.name: stage-manager-shortcut
key.description: Turns Stage Manager on or off. Empty means no shortcut; prefs has a button for Ctrl+Super+S.

key.name: stage-manager-new-windows
key.description: "replace": a new app window takes the stage and the previous set goes to the strip as one entry (macOS). "join": the new window joins the set on the stage. Alt-click an app (dock, app grid) to open it into the current stage once.

key.name: stage-manager-wallpaper-click
key.summary: Click the wallpaper to show the desktop
key.description: A click on the wallpaper sends the windows on the stage to the strip; another click brings them back.

key.name: stage-manager-tilt
key.description: How far, in degrees, the windows in the strip turn toward the stage. 0 lays them flat.

key.name: stage-manager-animation-speed
key.description: 1 is normal, 2 twice as fast, 0.5 half as fast. Reduced motion still replaces the moves with short fades.

key.name: stage-manager-remove-shortcut
key.description: Takes the focused window out of the set on the stage and puts it in the strip. Only active while Stage Manager is on.

key.name: stage-manager-show-recent
key.description: Show the strip of recent apps beside the stage. Off keeps it hidden until the pointer pushes against the screen edge (macOS "Show recent apps in Stage Manager").

key.name: stage-manager-strip-background
key.description: Draw a soft glass panel behind the strip of recent apps, so it reads apart from the app windows behind it. Off leaves the entries floating on the desktop (as macOS does).

key.name: stage-manager-next-shortcut
key.description: Puts the next set or app on the stage, in the order they were opened. Only active while Stage Manager is on.

key.name: stage-manager-previous-shortcut
key.description: Puts the previous set or app on the stage. Only active while Stage Manager is on.

key.name: stage-manager-slot-1-shortcut
key.description: Puts entry 1 of the strip (counted from the top) on the stage. Only active while Stage Manager is on.

key.name: stage-manager-slot-2-shortcut
key.description: Puts entry 2 of the strip (counted from the top) on the stage. Only active while Stage Manager is on.

key.name: stage-manager-slot-3-shortcut
key.description: Puts entry 3 of the strip (counted from the top) on the stage. Only active while Stage Manager is on.

key.name: stage-manager-slot-4-shortcut
key.description: Puts entry 4 of the strip (counted from the top) on the stage. Only active while Stage Manager is on.

key.name: stage-manager-slot-5-shortcut
key.description: Puts entry 5 of the strip (counted from the top) on the stage. Only active while Stage Manager is on.

key.name: stage-manager-slot-6-shortcut
key.description: Puts entry 6 of the strip (counted from the top) on the stage. Only active while Stage Manager is on.

key.name: launchpad
key.description: A full-screen grid of every app, with pages, search, folders and drag to reorder (macOS 11 to 15). Its folders and order are GNOME's own (org.gnome.desktop.app-folders and app-picker-layout), so the Activities app grid stays the same.

key.name: launchpad-shortcut
key.description: Opens and closes Launchpad. While Launchpad runs, GNOME's own "Show all apps" shortcut gives up these keys (Super+A by default) and gets them back when Launchpad stops. Empty means no shortcut.

key.name: launchpad-delete-apps
key.description: In jiggle mode (hold Alt, or press and hold an icon), show a delete button on apps their owner can remove: Only Flatpak apps (through GNOME Software). No other app gets one.

key.name: dock-launchpad
key.description: Show the Launchpad icon at the start of the Dock.

key.name: split-view
key.description: Tile a full-screen window to the left or right of the screen with a shortcut (split-view-left-shortcut, split-view-right-shortcut) and pick the window for the other half (macOS Split View). Esc cancels the pick; making a window of the pair full screen or maximized ends the pair.

key.name: split-view-left-shortcut
key.description: Tile the focused full-screen window to the left half and pick the window for the right half. Empty means no shortcut.

key.name: split-view-right-shortcut
key.description: Tile the focused full-screen window to the right half and pick the window for the left half. Empty means no shortcut.

key.name: mission-control
key.description: The overview becomes macOS Mission Control: a Spaces bar on top and the windows of the current Space spread out, with no search entry and no dash. App Exposé shows one app's windows.

key.name: mission-control-shortcut
key.description: Opens or closes Mission Control. F3 (and XF86LaunchA, the Mission Control key of Apple keyboards) and Control+Up, as on macOS.

key.name: app-expose-shortcut
key.description: Shows all windows of the front app, with its minimized windows along the bottom.

key.name: mc-static-spaces
key.summary: Keep Spaces until you remove them
key.description: Spaces stay as you made them, also when empty, and the Spaces bar has + and × buttons (macOS). GNOME's dynamic workspaces are off while this is on and come back after.

key.name: mc-rearrange-spaces
key.summary: Automatically rearrange Spaces based on most recent use
key.description: Mission Control puts the Spaces you used last first.

key.name: mc-group-by-app
key.description: Mission Control places the windows of one app next to each other.

key.name: mc-switch-to-app-space
key.summary: When switching to an application, switch to a Space with open windows for the application
key.description: Off: the app switcher only lists the windows of the current Space (GNOME's app-switcher current-workspace-only, given back when Guava stops).

key.name: mc-start-on-desktop
key.description: At login GNOME opens the overview; Guava shows the desktop instead, as macOS does.

key.name: show-desktop-button
key.summary: Show Desktop button in the top bar
key.description: A small top bar button that slides every window to the screen edges to show the desktop. Click it again, or click a window, to bring them back.

key.name: show-desktop-shortcut
key.description: Shows the desktop or brings the windows back. Empty means no Guava shortcut; GNOME's own Show Desktop shortcut, if set, also plays this animation while Guava runs.

key.name: click-wallpaper-reveals-desktop
key.description: Clicking empty wallpaper slides the windows aside to show the desktop (Stage Manager, while on, sends the stage to the strip instead): always (macOS), only while Stage Manager is on, or never. With desktop icons (DING) only clicks that reach the wallpaper count.

key.name: show-desktop-speed
key.description: How fast the windows slide aside and back: fast, normal or slow.

key.name: widgets
key.description: Widgets on the desktop, above the wallpaper and below windows. None are placed until you add some with Edit Widgets… (right-click the desktop).

key.name: widgets-layout
key.description: The placed widgets as JSON (kind, size, options, monitor and grid position). Empty means no widgets. Written by Guava when you add, move, resize or remove a widget.

key.name: widgets-style
key.description: automatic: monochrome and dimmed while an app window is in front, full colour when the desktop is. monochrome: always dimmed. full-color: never dimmed.

key.name: desktop-icons
key.description: Show the files and folders of your Desktop folder on the desktop, from the top-right corner as Finder does. Guava steps aside while the Desktop Icons NG extension (DING) is enabled.

key.name: desktop-icons-size
key.description: The size of the desktop icons in pixels, from 32 to 128. 64 is the macOS default.

key.name: desktop-icons-show-drives
key.summary: Show mounted drives on the desktop
key.description: Show USB sticks, memory cards, discs and other drives you mounted as icons on the desktop. Eject them from their right-click menu.

key.name: desktop-icons-sort
key.description: none: icons stay where you put them and new ones take the next free place. The others arrange every icon in that order, from the top-right corner down and then to the left. Dragging an icon sets it back to none.

key.name: desktop-icons-layout
key.description: Where each desktop icon sits, as JSON (the file name and its column and row from the top-right corner). Empty means no icon has been placed yet. Written by Guava when you drag icons or new files arrive.

key.name: screenshots
key.summary: macOS screenshot shortcuts, toolbar and thumbnail
key.description: Shift+Super+3 captures the screen, Shift+Super+4 an area or window, Shift+Super+5 opens the toolbar. They drive GNOME's own screenshot UI; Print and the other GNOME shortcuts stay as they are.

key.name: screenshots-shortcut-screen
key.description: Takes a screenshot of the whole screen at once. Empty means no shortcut.

key.name: screenshots-shortcut-selection
key.description: Drag an area to capture it; press Space to pick a window instead. Empty means no shortcut.

key.name: screenshots-shortcut-toolbar
key.description: Opens the toolbar with the capture and recording modes and Options. While a recording runs, it stops the recording. Empty means no shortcut.

key.name: screenshots-save-to
key.description: Pictures/Screenshots (GNOME's own folder), the Desktop, Documents, only the clipboard, or another folder. macOS saves to the Desktop.

key.name: screenshots-other-folder
key.description: The folder used when Save to is Other Location.

key.name: screenshots-timer
key.description: Waits this long after you click Capture or Record in the toolbar. Guava uses 0 (none), 5 or 10.

key.name: screenshots-thumbnail
key.description: After a capture a small preview slides in at the bottom right. The file is saved to your chosen folder after 5 seconds, or at once when you swipe the preview to the right.

key.name: screenshots-remember-selection
key.description: Starts the next area selection where the last one was.

key.name: screenshots-show-pointer
key.summary: Show the mouse pointer in captures
key.description: Includes the pointer in screenshots and recordings.

key.name: screenshots-macos-names
key.description: Names screenshots "Screenshot 2026-03-09 at 08.05.07" instead of GNOME's "Screenshot From ...".

key.name: screenshots-last-selection
key.description: The x, y, width and height of the last selected area. Guava writes it.

key.name: app-switcher
key.description: Super+Tab shows a panel of big app icons in most-recently-used order: Tab moves, Q quits, H hides, Down shows the app's windows, releasing Super switches. Replaces GNOME's app switcher while on; your shortcut is kept.

key.name: switcher-cycle-windows
key.summary: Super+` cycles the windows of the front app
key.description: Like Cmd-` on macOS: each press brings the next window of the current app forward, without a panel. Off gives Super+` back to GNOME's switcher.

key.name: switcher-switch-to-space
key.summary: Switch to a Space with open windows for the application
key.description: Choosing an app with no window on this workspace goes to a workspace that has one (macOS Mission Control setting). Off opens a new window here when the app can.

key.name: switcher-restore-minimized
key.summary: Switching to an app restores its minimized windows
key.description: macOS leaves minimized windows in the Dock unless Option (Alt) is held when Cmd (Super) is released. On restores the most recent one when the app has no other window to show.

key.name: gestures
key.description: macOS three- and four-finger touchpad gestures: App Exposé, Launchpad and Show Desktop, next to GNOME's own swipes for Mission Control and workspaces.

key.name: gestures-mission-control
key.summary: Swipe up with three or four fingers for Mission Control
key.description: GNOME's own overview swipe. Off: the swipe does nothing on the desktop.

key.name: gestures-spaces
key.summary: Swipe left or right with three or four fingers to switch Spaces
key.description: GNOME's own workspace swipe. Off: the swipe does nothing on the desktop.

key.name: gestures-app-expose
key.summary: Swipe down with four fingers for App Exposé
key.description: Shows every window of the front app.

key.name: gestures-launchpad
key.summary: Pinch with thumb and three fingers for Launchpad
key.description: Opens the Launchpad (the app grid).

key.name: gestures-show-desktop
key.summary: Spread with thumb and three fingers to show the desktop
key.description: Pushes the windows aside, like Show Desktop; pinch or click to bring them back.

key.name: hot-corner-top-left
key.description: What pushing the pointer into the top left corner does: none, mission-control, app-expose (Application Windows), desktop, notification-center, launchpad, lock-screen or display-sleep. macOS has every corner off.

key.name: hot-corner-top-left-modifier
key.summary: Modifier key the top left hot corner needs
key.description: The corner fires only while this key is held (none, shift, ctrl, alt or super), which avoids accidental triggers.

key.name: hot-corner-top-right
key.description: What pushing the pointer into the top right corner does: none, mission-control, app-expose (Application Windows), desktop, notification-center, launchpad, lock-screen or display-sleep. macOS has every corner off.

key.name: hot-corner-top-right-modifier
key.summary: Modifier key the top right hot corner needs
key.description: The corner fires only while this key is held (none, shift, ctrl, alt or super), which avoids accidental triggers.

key.name: hot-corner-bottom-left
key.description: What pushing the pointer into the bottom left corner does: none, mission-control, app-expose (Application Windows), desktop, notification-center, launchpad, lock-screen or display-sleep. macOS has every corner off.

key.name: hot-corner-bottom-left-modifier
key.summary: Modifier key the bottom left hot corner needs
key.description: The corner fires only while this key is held (none, shift, ctrl, alt or super), which avoids accidental triggers.

key.name: hot-corner-bottom-right
key.description: What pushing the pointer into the bottom right corner does: none, mission-control, app-expose (Application Windows), desktop, notification-center, launchpad, lock-screen or display-sleep. macOS has every corner off.

key.name: hot-corner-bottom-right-modifier
key.summary: Modifier key the bottom right hot corner needs
key.description: The corner fires only while this key is held (none, shift, ctrl, alt or super), which avoids accidental triggers.

key.name: clipboard-history
key.description: Keep a history of copied text, links, colours and images, with a top-bar popover and Quick Paste.

key.name: clipboard-recording
key.description: When off, nothing new is recorded and the existing history is kept.

key.name: clipboard-shortcut
key.description: Opens Quick Paste. Empty means no shortcut; prefs has a button for Super+Shift+V.

key.name: clipboard-panel-icon
key.summary: Clipboard icon in the top bar
key.description: Show the clipboard history popover button in the top bar.

key.name: clipboard-history-size
key.description: How many unpinned entries are kept. Pinned entries never count and never expire.

key.name: clipboard-images
key.description: Record images in the clipboard history. Images over 5 MB are skipped.

key.name: clipboard-persist
key.description: Save history in ~/.local/share/guava/clipboard/ (readable only by you) so it survives screen lock and log out. Turning it off deletes the saved files.

key.name: clipboard-ignore-sensitive
key.description: Do not record copies marked as secret (x-kde-passwordManagerHint) or copied from known password managers.

key.name: clipboard-excluded-apps
key.description: Extra window classes or application ids whose copies are never recorded.

key.name: spotlight
key.description: A centred search bar for apps, settings, files, the clipboard, calculations and the web.

key.name: spotlight-on-super
key.summary: Open Spotlight with a tap of Super
key.description: A tap of the Super key opens Spotlight instead of the Activities overview. The overview stays on the hot corner, the touchpad gesture, Super+A and the Activities button. Off gives the key back to the overview.

key.name: spotlight-shortcut
key.description: An optional extra shortcut that opens Spotlight, for example <Super>slash. Empty means none. Super+Space is left to GNOME's input-source switch.

key.name: spotlight-files
key.description: Show file results from GNOME's own search (Files). Guava does not index anything.

key.name: spotlight-settings
key.description: Show GNOME Settings panels and Guava switches in the results.

key.name: spotlight-calculator
key.description: Evaluate arithmetic and unit conversions typed in the search field.

key.name: spotlight-clipboard
key.description: Show recent Clipboard history entries. Needs Clipboard history to be on.

key.name: spotlight-recent-clipboard
key.summary: Spotlight: recent clipboard on an empty search
key.description: Show the latest Clipboard history entries when the search field is empty. Off by default so copied text is not shown to anyone glancing at the screen. Typing still searches the clipboard when Spotlight: clipboard is on.

key.name: spotlight-web
key.description: Add a row that opens your search engine in the browser. Nothing is sent until you press Return.

key.name: spotlight-engine
key.description: One of duckduckgo, google, bing, brave, startpage, ecosia, or an https address that contains %s for the search words.

key.name: spotlight-views
key.description: Show the Applications, Files, Actions and Clipboard buttons next to the empty search field, as on macOS Tahoe. Super+1 to Super+4 open them while Spotlight is open.

key.name: spotlight-actions
key.description: Search and run actions: Guava's own (Show Desktop, Lock Screen, a timer, Do Not Disturb, Dark Mode, Empty Trash, Take Screenshot) and the actions apps list in their .desktop files, such as New Private Window.

key.name: spotlight-quick-keys
key.description: Short aliases typed in Spotlight, as "alias=target". The alias is 1 to 12 lowercase letters or digits; the target is action:ID (show-desktop, lock, timer, dnd, dark-mode, empty-trash, screenshot) or app:DESKTOP-ID. Words after the alias are the action's parameter, as in "tm 5" for a 5-minute timer.

key.name: spotlight-history
key.description: Remember recent searches and opened results, shown when the field is empty and recalled with the Up arrow, as on macOS. Turning it off clears them.

key.name: spotlight-history-queries
key.description: The last searches that opened a result, newest first. Written by Spotlight; cleared by "Clear History".

key.name: spotlight-recent-results
key.description: The last opened results (apps, files, actions, settings) as small JSON records, newest first. Written by Spotlight; cleared by "Clear History".

key.name: spotlight-quick-look
key.description: Space on a selected file previews it with GNOME's previewer (Sushi), when it is installed.

key.name: spotlight-menu-items
key.description: Search the menu items of the focused app (from Guava's menu bar), and Tab scopes the search to them.

key.name: notch
key.description: Show notifications, live activities and volume or brightness changes in a pill at the top centre of the screen. Turning it off restores the standard banners and on-screen display. The notification history stays in the calendar menu.

key.name: notch-notifications
key.description: Show notification banners in the notch instead of the standard banner.

key.name: notch-live-activities
key.description: Show what is happening now, such as the playing song, in the notch.

key.name: notch-timeout
key.description: How long a notification stays in the notch. Hovering keeps it open and urgent ones stay until dismissed.

key.name: notch-show-clipboard
key.summary: Show clipboard in the notch dashboard
key.description: Show the latest clipboard entries in the notch dashboard, which opens when you click the notch. Turn it off to keep copied text off the screen while sharing it.

key.name: notch-hover-expand
key.description: Open the notch when the pointer rests on it, like the Dynamic Island apps on macOS. A click still opens it, and keeps it open.

key.name: notch-hover-delay
key.description: How long the pointer must rest on the notch before it opens.

key.name: notch-activity-battery
key.description: Show charging, low battery and accessory battery in the notch.

key.name: notch-activity-bluetooth
key.description: Show Bluetooth headphones when they connect, with their battery level.

key.name: notch-activity-timers
key.description: Show Guava timers counting down in the notch.

key.name: notch-activity-recording
key.description: Show a running screen recording in the notch, with a stop button.

key.name: notch-activity-calendar
key.description: Show the next calendar event in the notch from 15 minutes before it starts.

key.name: notch-activity-downloads
key.description: Show download progress in the notch (app progress bars and partial files in Downloads).

key.name: notch-copy-codes
key.description: When a notification carries a one-time code, offer a Copy button in the notch. Detection runs locally.

key.name: notch-shelf-downloads
key.description: Put each finished download on the notch shelf.

key.name: notch-shelf-screenshots
key.description: Put each new screenshot on the notch shelf.

key.name: notch-shelf
key.description: Internal. The file links on the notch shelf, newest first. Only links are kept; the files stay where they are.

key.name: timers-state
key.description: Internal. Guava's running and paused timers, so they survive the lock screen and a restart. Written by core/timers.js.

key.name: notification-center
key.description: Clicking the clock opens a column at the right of the screen with the date, the notifications grouped by app and the widgets, as on macOS. Off: the clock opens the calendar card.

key.name: notification-center-widgets
key.description: Show the widgets area below the notifications.

key.name: focus-modes
key.description: Do Not Disturb becomes one of several Focus modes (Do Not Disturb, Sleep, Work, Personal and custom ones), each with allowed apps, schedules and app triggers. The Control Center shows a Focus menu.

key.name: focus-profiles
key.description: JSON list of the Focus modes and their allowed apps, schedules and app triggers. Empty: the built-in modes with nothing allowed and nothing automatic (the macOS default).

key.name: focus-state
key.description: Written by Guava: the mode the user turned on, and until when, as JSON. Empty: the schedules and app triggers decide.

key.name: focus-last
key.description: Written by Guava: the mode a click on the Focus tile turns on.

key.name: focus-menubar-icon
key.summary: Show the Focus icon in the menu bar
key.description: Show the active Focus mode's icon in the top bar.

key.name: osd-location
key.description: 'notch' shows them in the notch while it is on, and in a glass pill under the menu bar when it is off (macOS 26 style); 'menu-bar' always uses the pill; 'system' keeps GNOME's centred pop-up.

key.name: dialogs-glass
key.description: Restyle the Shell's modal dialogs (authentication, log out, restart and shut down, Run a Command) as macOS-style glass alerts: an icon on top, buttons at the right, the default one in the accent colour.

key.name: color-filter
key.description: Filter every colour on screen, like macOS Accessibility > Display > Colour Filters. Off by default.

key.name: color-filter-kind
key.description: Greyscale, a correction for red/green (protanopia), green/red (deuteranopia) or blue/yellow (tritanopia) colour blindness, or a colour tint.

key.name: color-filter-intensity
key.description: How strongly the filter applies, in percent.

key.name: color-filter-hue
key.description: The hue of the colour tint filter, in degrees.
